title: Tanzanian Fish Curry
community: Enjoyed nationwide across coastal and inland Tanzania
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Mchuzi wa Samaki — fish in a rich tomato-onion sauce with Tanzanian spices. The tomato-based fish curry without coconut milk — lighter, sharper, deeply flavourful. Tanzania's most widely made fish stew.
longDesc: Mchuzi wa Samaki is the inland version of Tanzanian fish stew — lighter and sharper than the coconut milk version. The fish curry served at every mama lishe in Dar es Salaam, with ugali.
ingredients: 800g firm fish — tilapia, snapper, or catfish
steps: Season fish with salt and turmeric.
Cook onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, chillies, spices.
Add tomatoes. Cook until completely broken down — 8 minutes.
Add water. Simmer. Add fish. Cover and simmer gently 10—12 minutes.
chefTips: Tomato base must be fully reduced before adding fish.
cookingScience: Extended tomato cooking concentrates lycopene and glutamic acid — the umami compound that gives depth to the sauce.
sustainabilityTips: Local Tanzanian fish from coastal or lake fishermen.
culturalNote: Mchuzi wa Samaki is the fish curry of everyday Tanzania — the stew at every mama lishe counter in Dar es Salaam.
